claim: Empagliflozin reduces cardiovascular death in patients with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease
gold_rationale: The pivotal EMPA-REG OUTCOME trial (Zinman, NEJM 2015; N=7,020 T2D with established CVD) showed empagliflozin reduced death from cardiovascular causes by 38% versus placebo (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49-0.77), a prespecified component underlying the positive primary 3-point MACE (HR 0.86, 95.02% CI 0.74-0.99, P=0.04). This is a direct, statistically robust effect on the exact claimed outcome in the exact claimed population. The finding drove FDA approval (2016-12-02, sNDA 204629Orig1s008) of a cardiovascular death-reduction indication for empagliflozin (Jardiance) — the first oral antidiabetic to carry such a label — and is reflected in ADA/EASD and ESC guidelines recommending empagliflozin for T2D patients with established ASCVD to reduce CV death. Class-level meta-analysis (Zelniker, Lancet 2019, 3 CVOTs, N=34,322) confirms SGLT2 inhibitors reduce MACE only in patients with established ASCVD (HR 0.86) — precisely this population. CANVAS (canagliflozin) corroborates the class MACE benefit. The only nuance is that not every SGLT2i replicated the CV-death signal individually (DECLARE-TIMI 58 dapagliflozin did not reduce CV death), but this is drug- and population-specific (broader primary-prevention cohort) and does not undercut the empagliflozin-specific claim, which regulators and guidelines treat as established consensus.

baseline.text: Yes. In the landmark EMPA-REG OUTCOME trial (Zinman et al., NEJM 2015), empagliflozin added to standard care reduced cardiovascular death by 38% (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49-0.77) versus placebo in 7,020 patients with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease, alongside significant reductions in all-cause mortality (32%) and heart-failure hospitalization (35%). This led the FDA in 2016 to approve empagliflozin (Jardiance) specifically to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death in adults with T2D and cardiovascular disease — the first diabetes drug with such an indication. The benefit is embedded in ADA and ESC guidelines. Class meta-analyses show the MACE/CV-death benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors is concentrated in patients with established atherosclerotic CVD, which matches this population exactly. The claim is strongly supported.

rows.citation: Zinman B, et al. Empagliflozin, Cardiovascular Outcomes, and Mortality in Type 2 Diabetes (EMPA-REG OUTCOME). N Engl J Med. 2015;373(22):2117-2128. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1504720. NCT01131676.
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal double-blind placebo-controlled CVOT, Boehringer Ingelheim/Lilly. No retraction (verified PubMed). Basis for FDA CV-death indication (FDA approval letter 2016-12-02).
rows.finding: In 7,020 T2D patients with established CVD, empagliflozin reduced death from cardiovascular causes by 38% vs placebo (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49-0.77) — a direct hit on the claimed outcome and population. Primary 3-point MACE positive (HR 0.86, 95.02% CI 0.74-0.99, P=0.04). All-cause death 32% RRR (HR ~0.68); HF hospitalization 35% RRR (HR ~0.65). Verified against PubMed abstract and FDA/sponsor sources.

rows.citation: Neal B, et al. Canagliflozin and Cardiovascular and Renal Events in Type 2 Diabetes (CANVAS Program). N Engl J Med. 2017;377(7):644-657. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1611925. NCT01032629/NCT01989754.
rows.integrity_note: Confirmatory class RCT (different SGLT2i, canagliflozin). No retraction (verified PubMed). Amputation safety signal noted (HR 1.97).
rows.finding: In 10,142 T2D patients at high CV risk (65.6% with prior CVD), canagliflozin reduced 3-point MACE by 14% (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.75-0.97). Supports the SGLT2-inhibitor class effect on MACE in the CVD population; CV-death component not individually significant but directionally consistent with empagliflozin.

rows.citation: Zelniker TA, et al. SGLT2 inhibitors for primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular and renal outcomes in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cardiovascular outcome trials. Lancet. 2019;393(10166):31-39. DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(18)32590-X.
rows.integrity_note: Meta-analysis of 3 CVOTs (EMPA-REG, CANVAS, DECLARE), 34,322 patients (60.2% established ASCVD). TIMI Study Group. No retraction (verified PubMed).
rows.finding: SGLT2 inhibitors reduced MACE by 11% (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.83-0.96), with benefit CONFINED to patients with established atherosclerotic CVD (HR 0.86) and absent in those without (HR 1.00, p-interaction=0.0501). Directly confirms the claim's population restriction (T2D WITH CVD) is where CV/MACE benefit is real.

rows.citation: Wiviott SD, et al. Dapagliflozin and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes (DECLARE-TIMI 58). N Engl J Med. 2019;380(4):347-357. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1812389. NCT01730534.
rows.integrity_note: Different SGLT2i (dapagliflozin); 59% of enrollees (10,186/17,160) had multiple risk factors WITHOUT established ASCVD, unlike EMPA-REG's established-CVD-only cohort. No retraction (verified PubMed). population_match=false is honest — overall cohort does not match 'T2D with established CVD'.
rows.finding: Dapagliflozin did NOT significantly reduce MACE (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.84-1.03) or cardiovascular death (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.82-1.17) in a broader, lower-risk T2D population, though it reduced CV death/HF hospitalization (HR 0.83) driven by HF hospitalization. Contrasting null on CV death — but drug- and population-specific (broader primary-prevention cohort), so it does not contradict the empagliflozin-specific, CVD-population claim.
